related_questions.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Turkey?

text_blocks.snippet: No, U.S. citizens do not need a visa to enter Turkey for stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business. For stays longer than 90 days, or for purposes other than tourism or business (like work or study), a visa is required.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, U.S. citizens do not need a visa to enter Turkey for stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business

list.title: Visa-free entry for short visits:
list.snippet: U.S. citizens can enter Turkey without a visa for tourism or business purposes for a maximum of 90 days within a 180-day period.

list.title: Passport validity:
list.snippet: Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended entry date into Turkey.

list.title: Other requirements:
list.snippet: While a visa isn't required for short stays, you should still have a valid passport, and it's recommended to have proof of sufficient funds, a return or onward ticket, and travel insurance.

list.title: Longer stays or other purposes:
list.snippet: For stays longer than 90 days, or if you plan to work or study in Turkey, you will need to obtain the appropriate visa before traveling.

list.title: e-Visas:
list.snippet: For some nationalities, Turkey offers an e-visa system for short-term stays. While not required for U.S. citizens for tourism or business, it's available if you want to obtain one before traveling.

list.title: Important:
list.snippet: Always check the latest travel advisories and requirements from official sources like the U.S. Department of State and the Turkish government before your trip, as rules can change.

related_questions.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Thailand?

text_blocks.snippet: US citizens can generally enter Thailand without a visa for a stay of up to 60 days for tourism purposes. This is made possible through the Visa Exemption Scheme. You will need a valid passport and may need to show proof of onward or return travel and sufficient funds.
snippet_highlighted_words: US citizens can generally enter Thailand without a visa for a stay of up to 60 days for tourism purposes

list.snippet: Eligible for: US citizens traveling for tourism.
Stay Duration: Up to 60 days, with the possibility of extension for an additional 30 days at a Thai immigration office.
Entry Points: This applies to both air and land/sea border crossings.
Requirements:
Valid passport (at least six months validity beyond your intended stay).
Proof of onward or return travel within the permitted stay.
Sufficient funds to cover your stay (may be requested by immigration officials).
If you plan to stay longer than 60 days or for purposes other than tourism (e.g., work, study), you will need to apply for a specific Thai visa before traveling.
It is recommended to check with the Thai Embassy or Consulate for the most up-to-date information and specific requirements for your situation.

Starting May 1, 2025, all non-Thai nationals entering Thailand, including those under the Visa Exemption scheme, will need to complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 3 days of arrival.
